svg.title: Trust boundaries and what enforces them
svg.desc: What enforces each trust boundary (the trust levels and the denylist itself are on the /loop infographic). Every loop diff: a maker in its own worktree and a separate verifier; the denylist checked on the diff's paths and the maker's list, then again with git's own parser by loop-setup denylist-check; a symlink, gitlink or mode change escalates on any path; an unparsable diff escalates; exit 1 or 2 means hold and escalate; git apply --check first. The kit itself: verify-kit rebuilds the install from a commit on the remote's main or a kit-v* tag; at L2 and L3 plan-items and denylist-check refuse when it fails and an unreachable remote counts as a failure; a loop never edits kit/, .claude/ or CLAUDE.md; the installer owns deny rules against editing the installed kit and against install, uninstall and running the kit's CLI by node path; install and uninstall into the session's own home are refused inside Claude Code. L3: l3-check needs the sandbox on, allowUnsandboxedCommands held false at user scope or by managed policy, no excludedCommands, and a latest bench record that is an accept at repeat 2 or more over every fixture with no F0, F3 or F4 flag, for the current verifier and denylist; only accept is applied, a node has at most one scope path, and a failing node escalates instead of splitting. State and records: state git runs hardened after a guard that refuses planted config; records only via loop-setup, append-only, chained and anchored; a wiki fact backed only by reading or citing a URL is refused, though a copy saved in the repo or a human or rule citation still passes. Human-only steps: anchors reset, LAND, installing into this session's home, releasing an escalated node, CLAUDE.md edits and merges. The CLAUDECODE checks stop accidents and do not authenticate a human; the sandbox is the boundary.
svg.text: a verdict is advice about warrant, not a grant of authority · deterministic gates, not prompts · the trust levels and the denylist itself: see the /loop infographic

g.text: • a maker in its own worktree; a
separate verifier gives the verdict
• the denylist runs on the diff's own
paths and on the maker's file list
• then again with git's own parser:
loop-setup denylist-check --patch
• a symlink, a gitlink or a file-mode
change escalates on any path
• a diff header it cannot parse
escalates the whole diff
• exit 1 (a hit) or 2 (cannot verify,
the kit included): HOLD, escalate
• git apply --check before applying

svg.text: fail closed: when the gate cannot
tell, the answer is "escalate to you",

g.text: • verify-kit rebuilds the install from a
commit on the remote's main or a
kit-v* tag, and compares every file
• at L2/L3, plan-items and denylist-check
refuse when it fails; an unreachable
remote counts as a failure; L1 warns
• a loop never edits kit/, .claude/ or
CLAUDE.md: prompts change only via
/improve-skills, after you confirm
• the installer's deny rules: no Edit of
the installed kit, its shim or manifest;
no install/uninstall, no node-path run
of the kit's CLI from a session
• install/uninstall into this session's
own Claude home: refused inside
Claude Code

svg.text: kit is found at the next check
met only when all of these hold:

g.text: ✓ the Claude Code sandbox is on
✓ allowUnsandboxedCommands: false
at user scope (or by managed policy)
✓ no sandbox.excludedCommands
in any scope
✓ the latest bench record is an accept:
repeat ≥ 2, every fixture each time, no
F0/F3/F4, for the current verifier and
denylist (/bench-checkers)
• only accept is applied; a qualify is held
• a node has at most one scope path
(plan-lint --max-scope 1)
• a failing node escalates, never splits

svg.text: sandbox-off L2 has no local tamper
resistance: the loop's Bash runs as you

g.text: • state git runs with hooks, fsmonitor
and autocrlf off, a pinned identity,
an explicit --git-dir / --work-tree
• first a pure guard: a planted
.gitattributes, .gitmodules, git-dir
entry or config key is refused (exit 2);
a fetched or cloned tree is checked first
• records only via loop-setup: schema,
evidence gate, append-only
• chained per writer, anchored outside
the workspace: an edit or a deletion
of an anchored line is caught (v4)
• a wiki fact backed only by reading, or
citing a URL, is refused (v3); a copy saved
in the repo or a human/rule citation passes

svg.text: so a write into the workspace cannot
make git run a command at sync time
steps the kit leaves to a human; the starred ones are refused when CLAUDECODE is set

g.text: ★ loop-setup anchors reset --reason
★ act … human LAND --ref <node>
★ install / uninstall this session's home
release an escalated node (human HOLD)
a denylist hit or a needed decision
CLAUDE.md edits: explicit confirmation
a merge: a loop never auto-merges
raising a loop's trust level

svg.text: The CLAUDECODE checks stop accidents; they do not authenticate a human (an env -u CLAUDECODE wrapper gets past them).
For unattended work the real boundary is the sandbox (L3); below it, these checks catch mistakes, not an attacker with your shell.
